pitch_limitations.what_pitch_proves: two or more physically distinct voices, separated by far more than the within-speaker spread, in channel-separated audio
pitch_limitations.what_pitch_does_NOT_prove: that every speaker is identifiable. Median f0 groups these speakers by voice range; WITHIN a group the median difference is smaller than the measurement's own noise floor, so a hand-off between those two produces no reliable pitch jump. A turn-taking stage must not assume 'the speaker changed' == 'f0 jumped'.

criteria.name: at least two speakers with usable voicing
some speaker pair separated by >= 3x the within-speaker MAD sigma
criteria.detail: best separation 4.7 MAD sigmas (FEO072 vs MEE073, delta 103.53 Hz) in ami_sdm_EN2002a_turns.wav

criteria.name: f0 alone is bimodal: the 2-means centres sit >= 3x the pooled within-speaker MAD sigma apart (no labels used)
criteria.detail: best centre separation 5.17 pooled sigmas; dominant-speaker purity 0.7935 (bounded below 1.0 by construction -- each pitch group holds two speakers, see pitch_limitations)

criteria.name: headset channels differ (channel-separated speaker identity)
criteria.detail: best channel separation 5.4 MAD sigmas (FEO070 vs MEE073, delta 110.12 Hz)
